That being said, it is also important to put virtual currency in perspective as a payment

By way of comparison, according to information reported publicly, in 2012 Western

This relative volume of transactions becomes important when you consider that,
according to the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, the best estimate for the amount of
all global criminal proceeds available for laundering through the financial system in 2009 was

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires suspicious activity reporting by financial institutions, and the fact pattern does not identify any financial institution’s SAR obligation or a reportable suspicious transaction determination.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates that a financial institution report suspicious transactions to the Treasury (i.e., a SAR regime) and provides related protections. Key elements for applicability are: (1) the presence of a covered “financial institution” subject to BSA reporting rules, and (2) a suspicious transaction (or attempted transaction) that triggers the institution’s duty to report under implementing regulations. Here, the facts describe an individual customer (SYN_e941bf20) with multiple low-dollar transactions and a high risk rating, but they do not identify the involved financial institution(s), whether any institution detected the activity as suspicious, or whether a SAR filing obligation was triggered under the applicable thresholds/criteria. Therefore, it cannot be determined from the facts whether § 5318(g) requires suspicious activity reporting in this scenario. Contiguous phrase in answer: “§ 5318(g) requires suspicious activity”.
